# diagram-chart — Numbers as a bar and/or line chart.

Draw what the user describes after the command.

## Best for
- Comparing amounts
- Trends over time
- Before and after figures

## Template
Draw a Mermaid **xychart-beta**. Do not switch to another diagram type.

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "UK inflation (%)"
    x-axis [2021, 2022, 2023, 2024]
    y-axis "Percent" 0 --> 12
    bar [2.6, 9.1, 7.3, 2.5]
    line [2.6, 9.1, 7.3, 2.5]
```

- Titles and axis names in double quotes. X-axis categories in square brackets, separated by commas.
- The y-axis range must cover every value. Each `bar [...]` or `line [...]` has one number per category.
- Numbers only in the data lists: no units, % signs or thousands commas. Use `bar` and/or `line`.
- Only use figures from the conversation or sources; say in the explanation if any are estimates.

2. Copy the template's shape. Do not add `%%{init}%%` themes, HTML tags, emoji or styling; the renderer supplies the dark look.
3. Keep every label on one line. Inside quoted labels use single quotes, never double quotes.
4. Keep it readable: about 20 items at most.
5. After the block, write 2 to 4 plain-English lines saying what the diagram shows.

If the request is vague, draw the most useful interpretation rather than asking. If nothing follows the command, diagram the most recent topic in this conversation.

# diagram-timeline — Events laid out in date order.

Draw what the user describes after the command.

## Best for
- History and background
- A sequence of incidents
- Project milestones

## Template
Draw a Mermaid **timeline**. Do not switch to another diagram type.

```mermaid
timeline
    title NHS dental changes
    2006 : New dental contract
    2020 : Practices close in lockdown
    2024 : Recovery plan : New patient premium
```

- Every line is `period : event`, with ` : ` between extra events in the same period. Never use arrows (`→`, `->`).
- The period must not contain a colon: write `14.30`, not `14:30`. No `#` or `;` in the period.
- Optional `section Name` lines group periods. Keep events short.
